question.text: SEBI prescribes that the minimum application value for a book-built IPO should be in the range of __________, ensuring meaningful participation by retail investors.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI prescribes that the issuer must specify a minimum bid lot such that the minimum application value in a book-built IPO adheres to the SEBI-prescribed range of Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 15,000. This keeps retail participation meaningful while remaining affordable. The Trap: Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 20,000 and Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 25,000 are higher than SEBI's prescribed range. Candidates may confuse the minimum application value with the retail investor category limit of Rs. 2 lakhs. Note: Minimum application value for a book-built IPO = Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 15,000.
